[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Jane was born in 1802. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]] and [[Arthur-2480|Mary Arthur]].

  - The 1831 census records John Gray at Boveedy with exactly one male and one female, both Presbyterian. Jane was 28 and her known husband John Gray was 32. 1831 transcription (https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/Tamlaght/1831census.tsv)
  - Jno. Gray remained a Boveedy landholder in the 1833 tithe, confirming household continuity. 1833 tithe (https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/derry/tithe-applotments/tamlaght-o-crilly-parish.php)
  - Descendant evidence specifically states that Jane married John Gray in Ireland before emigrating to Kentucky. Their later burial grouping confirms the couple’s identities, though not their marriage date. Jane Glasgow
    (https://hiltner.com/mckeown/getperson.php?personID=I374&tree=tree1)

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-822]] is assessed at 98% (proved). John Glasgow and Mary Arthur’s family Bible includes Jane, born 5 October 1802, among the nine children after their 21 May 1798 marriage. John’s 20 March 1847 letter to Jane Glasgow Gray adds direct family context.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare the register hand/entry with associated correspondence or baptism.

Source basis already held: [https://hiltner.com/mckeown/histories/8479.jpeg Glasgow family Bible, family register of John Glasgow and Mary Arthur, original register image (https://hiltner.com/mckeown/histories/8479.jpeg); media description (https://hiltner.com/mckeown/showmedia.php?mediaID=532&medialinkID=726), McKeown and Shields Families; the collection is indexed at hiltner.com/mckeown (https://hiltner.com/mckeown/index.php), accessed 29 August 2026.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


A possible identification concerns Jane Glasgow. An 1874 indenture traces James Glasgow’s 2 October 1779 Newtown of Larne lease to a 25 February 1832 renewal to Anne and Jane Glasgow.<ref>Inspected historical source; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS54-77Q4-H record].</ref> Original recital inspected. It establishes title succession, not stated descent; James and both women’s identities remain unresolved. The identification remains uncertain.
